beats.story: My mom gave my room a thorough deep cleaning before I arrived, and the chemical fresh scent from the products she'd sprayed over every surface lingers. I threw out most of the stuff from my old apartment. I don't want to surround myself with those things, those memories, again. Everything I was afraid would happen happened. Yet relief is what rules me somehow. I inhale the lemon disinfectant and let it cleanse my lungs with carcinongens. I pull the lid off one of the few boxes I've brought upstairs. Inside sits Miley's zebra and the envelope from Cliff she'd given me as I left.
beats.story_cn: 我回来前，我妈已把我的房间彻底消毒了一遍。她喷在每个角落的化学清洁剂，那股清新的气味至今仍萦绕不散。旧公寓的家当我扔了大半，我不想再被那些物品、那些回忆团团包围。我曾恐惧发生的一切，终究还是发生了。但不知怎的，主宰我的竟是一种解脱。我深吸一口呛人的柠檬消毒剂，任凭这致癌物冲洗肺叶。掀开为数不多几个搬上楼的纸箱盖，迈莉的斑马玩偶静静躺在里面，还有克里夫在我离开时交给我的那个信封。

beats.story: Things forgotten in your desk is printed in his writing on the front. Recycling it would be nothing at all. If I do that, I can move on to all the things I've actually planned to do this afternoon: setting up my room, going with my mom to the store to get new things, researching programs at local universities. If I open this now, it would mean going back to that cubicle, back to that person. I stare at it for too long. Finally, just as I've decided to take it to the bin, my mom calls my name from downstairs and I whip around, my arm hitting the envelope and spilling its contents onto the floor. I bend down to gather it. It's just napkins, Post-it notes that have lost their stickiness, old receipts.
beats.story_cn: 信封正面是他手写的“办公桌遗忘物”字样。把它扔进回收站毫不费力。若真这么做了，我就能继续执行下午计划好的所有事项：布置房间，陪妈妈去商场置办新物，查阅本地大学的研究项目。若现在打开它，便意味着要回到那个隔间，回到那个人。我盯着它看了太久。终于，正当我决定把它丢进废纸篓时，妈妈在楼下唤我的名字。我猛地转身，手臂横扫过信封，里面的东西哗啦洒了一地。我弯腰拾捡，不过是些餐巾纸、粘性尽失的便利贴、陈旧的收据。

beats.story: But my heartbeat halts as I pick up the first item: the Post-it note I'd grabbed off the donut box Cliff brought for the whole office that reads Not Poison ;). Next is the sketch he made to show me the set of Kidstreet. The napkin with the name Robin Winters written on it, from when we got milkshakes. The receipt from my bowling shoe rental. The ticket stub from the movies. Why was I such a pack rat? I put all these things in that bottom drawer because they didn't feel like garbage. They all meant so much to me.
beats.story_cn: 但当我拾起第一件物品时，心跳骤停：那是我从克里夫带给全办公室的甜甜圈盒上撕下的便利贴，上面写着“非毒药 ;)”。接着是他画给我看的《儿童街》布景草图。写着“罗宾·温特斯”的餐巾纸，来自我们同去喝奶昔的那次。保龄球馆租鞋的收据。电影票根。我过去怎会像个仓鼠囤粮一样？我把所有这些塞进底层抽屉，因为它们感觉不像垃圾。它们都曾是我生命里实实在在的重量。

beats.story: Last time we spoke, he was reaching out to me -- despite everything I did -- and I turned him away. Why would he give me another chance? After watching my phone obsessively for a full hour, I accept that no reply is coming. It's time to move on. So I go downstairs to join my mom and get on with all the errands we planned for the day. But late at night, as I'm brushing my teeth, my phone buzzes. Only one word sits on the screen, but I exhale with relief. My favorite word.
beats.story_cn: 上次交谈，他主动联系了我——尽管我做了那些事——而我却将他推开。他为何要再给我一次机会？对着手机痴守了整整一小时后，我终于接受不会有回音的事实。是时候往前看了。于是我下楼与母亲会合，着手处理我们计划了一天的所有琐事。但深夜刷牙时，手机突然一震。屏幕上只有一个词，我却如释重负地呼出一口气。那是我最爱的那个词。

The place is mostly empty, and the only sound is the buzz of the refrigerators. One bored-looking teen in a retro all-white creamery uniform stares at his phone behind the counter. Cliff's already sitting at the booth in the back, two Tiger-Tastic shakes waiting.
beats.story_cn: 奶昔？我能行。推开那扇冰激凌甜筒形状的门时，我只需要深呼吸，把心口发紧的感觉压下去。这里是Cliff。就算搞砸了也没关系。店里几乎空无一人，只有冰箱嗡嗡作响。柜台后，一个穿着复古全白制服的倦怠少年盯着手机。Cliff已经坐在后面的卡座里，两杯“虎啸特调”奶昔静候在桌上。

"Hey, Jolene," Cliff says when I reach him and lower myself into the seat across from him. He gives me a tentative stare, like he's not sure what I'll do next. "Hey, Cliff." I return a wobbly grin. There's so much to say. But being near him .
beats.story_cn: 他穿着有领衬衫，新剪的头发抹了少许发蜡。如此完美的Cliff风格。我颤巍巍走过去时，他的目光迎了上来。“嘿，Jolene，”我在他对面坐下，他试探地开口，眼神带着不确定，似乎猜不透我下一秒会做什么。“嘿，Cliff。”我回以一个摇摇欲坠的笑容。有太多话想说，但靠近他……

beats.story: He puts a hand to his chest and his lips part just a little. "This is amazing." "I think I owe you at leas -- " "No outside food!" the tired teen shouts from behind the ice-cream counter. "Honestly, I did not expect them to care," I say, and we both chuckle as Cliff closes the lid and pushes the box to the end of the table. "So," I start. "It's official. You're off the Supershops books." Cliff brightens. "Now we can say what we really think of that place." The curl of his lips, the brightness in his eyes -- they feel like home. "Did you end up changing your pick for who you'd kill for a billion dollars?" Cliff quirks his lip.

beats.story_cn: “噢，肯定是格雷戈里。我想他也心知肚明。我们分手时可不太愉快。我辞职前可是给总部递了份‘精彩’的报告。”想到格雷戈里将被自己崇拜的集团机器碾压，一阵快意窜过脊背。“新工作什么时候入职？”我问。他喝了一口奶昔才回答：“下周。”他面色红润，谈起未来时热情洋溢：“我真的超级兴奋。跟超级商店完全不一样。”

His grin turns teasing. "Seems like the mass layoffs made some people recognize a major need for more employee protections." "Clifford!" I pull my hand to my chest.
beats.story_cn: “这次我将聚焦于那些尚未建立员工自决机制的大企业。”他朝我扬了扬眉，“我将赋能他们组织起来进行谈判。”“太棒了。”我说。这工作太适合他了，他在原机构会快乐得多。我啜饮一口奶昔，压下翻涌的空虚感。克里夫继续道：“事实上，我将要会见的部分人员正是超级商店集团的雇员。”他的笑容变得促狭：“看来大规模裁员让某些人意识到，亟需加强员工保护机制。”“克里福德！”我按住胸口。

beats.story: "Are you being a hero?" His sheepish smile, I missed it -- and I'm going to miss it so much. "I can't help it," he says. "That job was the wrong fit, but it helped me find the right one." He's right, and a deeper part of me is genuinely happy for him. "That's really great." I look out the window, toward the gas station across the street. The one he told me his grandma used to work at. "Is Grace happy you're moving back to Vancouver?" Cliff shakes his head. "Jolene, I wasn't clear. I'm working for my old company, but the projects will be here." "What?" My chest swells, afraid to hope.
beats.story_cn: "你在逞英雄吗？"他那腼腆的笑容，我错过了——而且会非常想念。"我忍不住，"他说，"那份工作不合适，但它帮我找到了合适的。"他是对的，我内心深处真心为他高兴。"那真是太好了。"我望向窗外，街对面的加油站，就是他曾告诉我他奶奶工作过的那个。"格蕾丝知道你搬回温哥华会高兴吗？"克利夫摇摇头。"乔琳，我没说清楚。我为老公司工作，但项目会在这里。""什么？"我的胸口发胀，不敢抱有希望。

"We agreed to be completely honest from now on?" He says it like a question as he leans closer. "Are we okay just being friends? Has it ever worked for us?" I swallow down the lump in my throat. It feels impossible, but I've wanted to tell him for so long. I thought I never would get the chance.
beats.story_cn: "我不搬走，我们不在超级商店了。我们从这里开始怎么办？""我们可以试着重新做朋友？"我问。他的目光移到桌上的甜甜圈盒，然后重新锁定在我身上。"我们说好从此完全诚实？"他靠近说，像在提问。"我们能只做朋友吗？我们成功过吗？"我咽下喉咙里的哽咽。感觉不可能，但我已想告诉他太久。我以为我永远没机会了。

beats.story: "Cliff, I like you more than anyone else." His smile is instantaneous, so bright it hurts to see. "I know." His lips quiver with emotion. "I emptied your desk drawer, remember? I know exactly how you feel. You're maybe a little obsessed with me?" I mock flick his straw. "You're the one who showed up at the office at midnight, who came to my apartment -- and that was all sweet, but I'm just saying . . ." He leans farther across the table, and I'm like a sunflower to my light as I tilt to meet him halfway.
beats.story_cn: “克里夫，我比任何人都更喜欢你。”他的笑容瞬间绽放，耀眼得几乎刺痛了眼。“我知道。”他的唇因情绪而轻颤，“我清空了你的办公桌抽屉，记得吗？我清楚你的心意。你……也许对我有点痴迷？”我故意轻弹了一下他的吸管，“半夜来办公室找我的是你，跑去我公寓的也是你——那些都很甜蜜，但我只是说……”他将身子更倾过来，而我如同向日葵趋光本能般倾向他，迎合着这个距离。

beats.story: "I'm not in a good place to date right now. I'm still pretty much a mess." I let out a sigh, but the next part feels easier to say. "I'm working on myself." He doesn't let go of my hand as the words settle between us. "Yeah, that's . . . that sounds like the right thing." He lets the hurt in his voice slip through a crack. "I'm really happy for you." I know he means it, but this can't be it for us.
beats.story_cn: “我现在没心力约会。我还是一团糟。”我轻叹一声，但接下来的话却更容易出口：“我在努力调整自己。”他没有松开我的手，话语在我们之间沉沉落下。“嗯，这……听起来是对的。”他声音里泄露一丝痛楚，“我真心为你高兴。”我知道他是认真的，但我们的故事不该止步于此。

beats.story: I can't let him go again. So I say, "But maybe we can meet up again? I might need advice from an HR professional about finding a part-time job, college courses, career things. Is that what HR does?" "Yes. You finally got one right." A small spark lights in his eyes. "But for good measure, we should plan to meet up more than once. We might need a few sessions." I nod. "Sounds reasonable." He pulls out his phone.
beats.story_cn: 我不能再放手让他离开。于是我说：“但也许我们可以再见？关于找兼职、大学课程、职业规划的事，或许我需要HR专业人士的建议。HR负责这些吗？”“没错，这次你总算说对了。”他眼中闪过一点微光，“不过保险起见，我们应该多约几次。可能需要几番长谈。”我点头：“听起来合理。”他掏出了手机。
